subject: Next steps: FinTechX integration patterns & tool call error strategy
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria@fintechx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-04T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + proposed patterns from today’s integration call

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on the integration/architecture patterns FinTechX asked about (SDK setup, auth, routing, structured output/tool calling, embeddings/rerankers).

Quick recap (call highlights):
- FinTechX will run Redwood in Dedicated mode (initially) and needs: short tail latency (<= 120ms token p95), strict key rotation, and isolated KV cache per-customer.
- Two primary workloads: (1) transactional prompts for account support (low context, high QPS) and (2) nightly reranking/embeddings for fraud scoring (batch).

Proposed patterns (high level):
1) SDK + Auth: use our server-side SDK for core requests; front-end sends a short-lived session token to backend which then calls Redwood with per-customer auth. Recommend KMS-backed customer keys and rotating session tokens.
2) Routing: implement policy-based routing — latency-sensitive traffic -> low-latency pool; batch rerank -> quantized model pool. Fall back to compatible model variant on capacity pressure.
3) Tool/function calling: define explicit tool specs (see appendix) for account lookup, transaction enrichment, and DB writes. Prefer single-responsibility tool definitions; allow parallel invocation for enrichment (fan-out) with a bounded timeout and circuit-breaker.
4) Structured output: use JSON schema enforcement at the SDK level and validate before persisting. Provide a small schema registry for FinTechX objects.
5) Embeddings & rerank: recommended flow is daily batch embedding job into vector DB + on-request rerank via lightweight reranker model; keep embeddings 1536-d float16 quantized for cost.

Open questions we committed to follow up on:
- Exact session token TTL and rotation cadence (FinTechX security).
- Retention policy for prefix/KV cache per-customer.
- Failure mode expectations for parallel tool fan-out (partial success semantics).

Attachments: architecture map and auth flow (ftx-map_v1.png, redwood-auth-flow.pdf).

Next steps / owner: 
- Maria to confirm security TTL and any compliance constraints (action: Maria) — due 2027-05-06.
- Dev to draft example tool definitions and error-handling strategy (action: Dev Patel) — due 2027-05-05.
- Karthik to propose routing policies & capacity bands (action: Karthik) — due 2027-05-07.

If that looks right I’ll convert this into a one-page mutual action plan and share the MAP link.

Thanks,
Rachel

Subject: Re: Recap + proposed patterns from today’s integration call

Thanks Rachel — solid recap. A few clarifying questions and notes from our side: 

1) Session token TTL: security prefers short TTLs (<= 5 minutes) for session tokens issued to the front-end; backend-to-Redwood key rotation can be daily. Would that break any of your SDK assumptions?
2) Partial success semantics: for the fan-out enrichment, we need a clear contract. If 2/3 enrichment calls succeed, we want deterministic graceful degradation (mark missing fields and proceed) rather than failing the whole response.
3) Can you provide an example tool definition that includes error codes and retry semantics? That will help our API team map errors to our circuit-breakers.

We’ll confirm retention requirements for logs and KV cache after checking with compliance. For now assume 90 days unless we hear otherwise.

Also looping in Chris from our API team to help with routing questions.

—Maria
Maria Lopez

Subject: RE: Recap + proposed patterns from today’s integration call (tool defs + error model)

Hi — wrote up a compact example and a recommended error/timeout model. Pasting inline; attaching fuller docs (redwood-auth-flow.pdf) and a stub MAP.

--- example tool definition (JSON-like pseudo) ---
Tool: account_enrich
- inputs: {account_id, transaction_id}
- outputs: {name, risk_score, linked_accounts}
- timeout: 300ms
- retries: up to 1 (idempotent) with exponential backoff
- error codes: 400 (bad input), 404 (not found), 429 (upstream rate limit), 5xx (transient)
- partial_fallback: true (consumer may accept empty/missing fields when downstream returns 5xx or timeout)

Fan-out pattern recommendation:
- Launch parallel enrichment calls with a global budget of 350ms. Use the first N responses up to consistency level; tag missing fields as null and attach a metadata flag 'partial_enrichment=true'.
- Circuit breaker: trip after 5 failures in 1 minute per downstream. On open, route to cached enrichment or best-effort single-tool path.

Auth implications for 5-minute TTL session tokens:
- SDK will mint short-lived ephemeral tokens for front-end; backend uses long-term customer key stored in KMS to mint. SDK supports 5-minute TTLs (we recommend a refresh-on-interaction pattern to avoid expired tokens mid-request).

Routing & model fallback:
- Policy engine rule example: if request.p95_target < 120ms AND request.type=="txn", route->low-latency-pool; else if batch_rerank request -> quantized-rerank-pool. On capacity shortage, fallback to closest compatible model (same family, higher quantization).

Attachments included: redwood-auth-flow.pdf (detailed auth flow), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (blank MAP).

Action items:
- Dev to publish example tool JSON and a sample SDK snippet by EOD 2027-05-05 (in progress).
- Karthik to add routing policy examples to the shared Drive.
